The term "pious" refers to a person who is deeply religious or spiritual, while "egoist" refers to someone who is primarily concerned with their own interests and desires. When combined, "pious egoist" suggests that an individual is using their religious or spiritual beliefs as a way to justify or rationalize their own selfish desires.

In other words, a pious egoist is someone who uses their faith or spirituality to justify their own self-serving actions, rather than genuinely seeking to serve others or live a life of selflessness and compassion.
